problem.text: Sidorenko-type inequalities on Cayley-type bipartite kernels of finite groups and their conjugacy-class averages.

claims.text: Proposition 3.1: every bipartite graph satisfies the inequality on the conjugacy-class average of the indicator of a product of two subgroups. Theorem 1.3: if the density of H on every Cayley-type host is at least its density on the conjugacy-class average, then H is strong Sidorenko. Theorem 1.4: every 1-subdivision, hence every even subdivision, satisfies the inequality on conjugacy-averaged Cayley kernels of arbitrary real functions on finite groups.

assumptions.text: Szegedy's reduction in its Cayley form (Proposition 1.2); representation theory of finite groups.

methods.text: Fourier expansion over irreducible unitary representations; class functions have scalar Fourier coefficients; averages over vertices give commuting orthogonal projections, so each term is a trace of a product of two projections.

limitations.text: The positive results hold on conjugacy-averaged kernels only; the comparison hypothesis of Theorem 1.3 is not proved for any class of graphs beyond these.

relevance.text: No result of this paper decides the statement or a declared neighbour. For the 1-subdivision neighbours, Theorem 1.4 extends the abelian result to class-function Cayley kernels on all finite groups; it does not cover general hosts, which by Proposition 1.2 would need arbitrary Cayley kernels.
